This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988') has been filed by the appellants / claimants aggrieved by award dated 16/10/2017 passed in claim case No.48/2017 by the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rajnandgaon, District - Rajnandgaon (CG)

sentences.text: 2. Facts of the case in brief is that the deceased - Murharam was driving the offending vehicle (motor cycle) bearing registration No.CG 08 ZD-0150 which was owned by him and insured with respondent No.1.
On the date of incident, i.e. 24/02/2016, the deceased was coming from village - Kodabadi to his home, some animal came on his way and his motor cycle dashed to a tree.

Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16768 Due to the said accident, he sustained injuries and succumbed to death.
3.
As per claim application, the deceased was aged about 35 years and was earning Rs.3,000/- and the claimants / appellants were depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
They claimed total amount of Rs.11,45,000/- as compensation.
Respondent / Insurance Company denied the averments of the claim application and stated that the deceased died due to his own negligence.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the findings of learned Tribunal are contrary to the evidence and liable to be set aside.

He submits that as per pleadings of the claim application, premium of Rs.50/- was charged for owner - driver of the offending vehicle, therefore,
his risk was covered under the policy and dismissal of the claim application holding that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased is liable to be set aside.

He placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramkhiladi and another v.
The United Insurance Co. Ltd. and another

entities.text:
Ramkhiladi and another v.
The United Insurance Co. Ltd. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550 and submits that since the additional premium to cover the owner-driver was charged by the Insurance Company, Rs.1 lakh ought to have been awarded.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent / insurance company submits that the deceased was the owner of the offending vehicle and therefore, his claim application is not maintainable.
In the case in hand, the driver himself was negligent and he cannot claim compensation for his own negligence.

He further submits that the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal with regard to negligence on the part of the deceased himself and rejection of the claim application is based upon proper appreciation of evidence, material available on record and it does not require any interference.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.
7. There is no dispute to the fact that the deceased himself was driving the offending vehicle and he was the owner / insured of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the record, it appears that in the insurance policy, premium of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16768 Rs.50/- was charged for compulsory P.A. cover (owner - driver).
In the case of Ramkhiladi (supra), it was held as under - "9.5.

It is true that, in a claim under Section 163-A of the Act, there is no need for the claimants to plead or establish the negligence and/or that the death in respect of which the claim petition is sought to be established was due to wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle concerned.

It is also true that the claim petition Smt. Basantin Bai vs The Branch Manager on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42493711/
2 under Section 163-A of the Act is based on the principle of no-fault liability.

entities.text: Basantin Bai vs The Branch Manager on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
at the same time, the deceased has to be a third party and cannot maintain a claim under Section 163-A of the Act against the owner and insurer of the vehicle which is borrowed by him as he will be in the shoes of the owner and he cannot maintain a claim under Section 163-A of the Act against the owner and insurer of the vehicle bearing registration No.RJ 02 SA 7811.
In the present case, the parties are governed by the contract of insurance and under the contract of insurance the liability of the insurance company would be qua third party only.
In the present case, as observed hereinabove, the deceased cannot be said to be a third party with respect to the insured vehicle bearing registration No. RJ 02 SA 7811.
There cannot be any dispute that the liability of the insurance company would be as per the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

As held by this Court in the case of Dhanraj v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and anr. reported in (2004) 8 SCC 553, an insurance policy covers the liability incurred by the insured in respect of death of or bodily injury to any person (including an owner of the goods or his authorized representative) carried in the vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle.

entities.text: Dhanraj v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, it is further held by this Court that Section 147 does not require an insurance company to assume risk for death or bodily injury to the owner of the vehicle."
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16768 8.

Admittedly, in this case, the deceased was the owner of the offending vehicle and he was not a 3rd party and his risk was covered under the contract of insurance policy only to the extent of Rs.1 lakh.

Hence, in the light of above judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, as the deceased was the owner of the offending vehicle, appellants/claimants are only entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
with 6% interest from the date of claim application till its realization.
Hence, the appeal is allowed in part and the impugned award is set aside.
The impugned award is modified to the above extent.
Consequence to follow.
